description: A scanner's alert about a vulnerability in a repository, a VM or a container image, such as from Aikido, Dependabot, Socket or Snyk, and its status there. Large scans travel as a record set.

advisory.description: The canonical advisory id, GHSA-… or CVE-….

advisory_aliases.description: The advisory's other ids, such as the CVE for a GHSA advisory, so a rule written with either matches.

affected_file.description: The vulnerable file, such as a library's path on a VM.

ecosystem.description: Such as npm, cargo or pypi.

id.description: <scanner>-<the scanner's alert id>, such as dependabot-412. When one scanner alert covers several targets, as a Socket alert can, there is a record for each target, with id <scanner>-<alert id>-<target>, the target being its id lowercased with each run of other characters a hyphen, such as socket-1474-acme-api.

reachability.description: The scanner's analysis of whether the vulnerable code can be reached, when it gives one. Across several locations, such as branches, it is unreachable only if every location is, and otherwise the most reachable value, reachable before unknown. A scanner value that says the code may be reached maps to reachable, and one that says the analysis couldn't decide maps to unknown; the scanner's own value goes in source_fields.

reachability_history.description: Each reachability the scanner has reported and when it started, oldest first, as far as the publisher has seen; one entry per change, not per scan. The last entry is the current reachability. Only with reachability. A publisher's first export starts it with one entry.

scanner.description: The scanner, in lowercase, such as aikido, dependabot, socket or snyk. (Not source, which is where every record says what it was built from.)

source_fields.description: The source's own fields that no field here covers, under the source's names. Readers keep it and don't interpret it. Never a personal value that a field here would label.

id.description: For a reader to match exactly against what it holds, such as system github and id acme/api, or system aikido and id 70001 for a VM. For a container image, the image repository without a tag or digest, such as ghcr.io/acme/api, so each build is the same target; seen_in says which build.

name.description: How to show it, such as a VM's hostname.

seen_in.description: The latest version of the target the scanner found it in, so a reader can skip a finding whose version is no longer running. At least one field; an empty branches doesn't count.

branches.description: A repository's branches it is still present on, such as main and dev. One record covers them all.

digest.description: A container image's digest, in the registry's own form.

tag.description: A container image's tag, such as 1.4.2. Tags move; a digest is exact.

url.description: The alert in the scanner's own interface.

title: vulnerability-alert
